description: ASIMeC is a content analysis scheme developed by the authors to identify message characteristics along five dimensions: moderating, summarising, adding new discussion points, adding theory, and adding external information.
title: ASIMeC analysis scheme for coding message characteristics and role adoption

description: The article proposes that assessment metadata — data about how students behave on a test or survey, including disengagement indicators — can function as naturally occurring, direct measures of social-emotional competencies, offering an alternative to deliberately administered SEL surveys.
title: Assessment metadata as naturally occurring direct SEL measurement

description: The report's central recommendation is that method choice should be driven by the alignment between an estimator's assumptions and the study's goals rather than by the design-based versus model-based label, since the empirical differences were small.
title: Assumption- and estimand-aligned estimator selection for education impact evaluations

description: Asymdystopia is the authors' named concept for a context in which increasing sample size does not improve, and can worsen, inference.
title: Asymdystopia
